UnitStatement: The pdf2md-page-assets skill is normally spawned by the PDF2MD orchestrator after page transcription and cleanup.
A page-assets task reads one page raster and its clean Markdown context.
A page-assets task identifies visible figures, tables, and other meaningful images.
The brief-schema task list says page-assets emits bbox-normalized asset records and table CSV text per the skill contract.
Notes: Conflicts with later SKILL and QA text that removes legacy csv_text in favor of table_data.

UnitStatement: The TaskSkill field must match the pdf2md-page-assets skill folder name.
RuntimeOverrides.IMAGE_PATH must be an existing absolute path to a page PNG.
RuntimeOverrides.PAGE_MD_PATH must be an existing absolute path to clean page Markdown.
RuntimeOverrides.OUTPUT_PATH must be an absolute path to the page asset JSON with an existing parent directory.
RuntimeOverrides.DOC_STEM is used for context only because deterministic tools assign final IDs.
RuntimeOverrides.PAGE_NUM is a positive 1-indexed page number.
RuntimeOverrides.TOTAL_PAGES must be a positive integer greater than or equal to PAGE_NUM.
RuntimeOverrides.ASSET_POLICY defaults to prose-document-assets-v1 and is echoed into JSON.
The pdf2md-page-assets skill runs with TaskProfile NONE in generic TASK shell mode.
The brief-schema read boundary limits reads to IMAGE_PATH and PAGE_MD_PATH only.
The skill must not read neighbouring page images, manifests, sibling Markdown, or public asset folders.
The brief-schema write boundary limits writes to OUTPUT_PATH only.
AllowedTools should be omitted because the skill is VLM-reasoning-only with no deterministic tool dependencies.
The orchestrator should prefer tools/pdf2md/build_page_assets_brief.py to build page-assets briefs.
The page-assets brief-builder emits the required INIT-TASK shape and reduces prompt drift.
CustomInstructions are usually unnecessary and should remain run-specific when used.
CustomInstructions should not restate the whole skill contract.
A run-specific instruction may classify cover-page publisher marks as img rather than fig.
For tables, captions should include the visible title or caption and must not invent units.
When a table spans beyond the page, the worker should extract only visible rows and add a possible_continuation issue.
A missing IMAGE_PATH or non-PNG IMAGE_PATH requires FAILED_INPUTS.
A missing PAGE_MD_PATH or non-Markdown PAGE_MD_PATH requires FAILED_INPUTS.
The OUTPUT_PATH parent directory must exist before the skill writes output.
The OUTPUT_PATH must exist after the run and be non-empty.
The page asset output must parse with json.loads.
The worker may read no files other than IMAGE_PATH and PAGE_MD_PATH.
The worker may write no files other than OUTPUT_PATH.
The output JSON must include schema_version with value pdf2md-page-assets/v1.
The output JSON run_status must be SUCCESS, NO_ASSETS, FAILED, or FAILED_INPUTS.
The output JSON doc_stem, page, and total_pages fields echo their runtime overrides.
The output JSON asset_policy field echoes ASSET_POLICY or its default.
The output JSON assets and issues fields are lists that may be empty.
Each asset kind must be exactly fig, tbl, or img.
Asset kind aliases such as figure, image, table, diagram, plot, chart, logo, or photo are rejected downstream.
Alternate asset keys type and subtype are rejected downstream.
Asset ordinal must be a positive integer within page and kind reading order.
Asset caption must be the visible caption or a concise visual description.
The only accepted asset caption field name is caption.
Asset slug is a short ASCII-friendly advisory slug or blank when uncertain.
Asset bbox_norm must be four numbers [x0, y0, x1, y1] in normalized top-left-origin coordinates.
Each bbox_norm coordinate must be in [0, 1], with x0 less than x1 and y0 less than y1.
bbox_norm must be a JSON array, not a dictionary with x0, y0, x1, and y1 keys.
Asset confidence must be high, medium, or low.
A legible tbl asset requires table_data conforming to the pdf2md-table/v1 schema.
Legacy csv_text and table_csv fields are rejected by materialize_page_assets.py.
A visible tbl that cannot be safely transcribed requires needs_extraction as a boolean.
When needs_extraction is used for a table, table_data must be omitted and an issue such as table_unreadable must be present.
A table_data block must declare schema_version exactly as pdf2md-table/v1.
table_data.rows must be a non-empty JSON array of rows shaped as objects with cells arrays.
table_data.header_rows must be an integer from 0 through the number of rows.
Every table_data.section_dividers index must be in the range [0, len(rows)).
Each table cell must include value.
Cell row_span and col_span values, when present, must be integers greater than or equal to 1.
Cell type, when present, must be text, number, fraction, missing, formula, or boolean.
Cell is_header, when present, must be boolean.
Every cell footnote_markers entry must appear in the table-level footnotes marker set.
No row_span may extend across a section_dividers boundary.
continuation_of must be null or an object with doc_stem, page, and tbl_ordinal.
The output JSON top level must be an object rather than a list or scalar.
Missing the top-level assets key is a strict shape defect.
Top-level sibling keys tables, figures, or images are rejected because the canonical shape is a flat assets array.
The top-level assets field must be a JSON array.
The page-number field is page, not page_num.
Inline asset placeholders are emitted by pdf2md-page, not pdf2md-page-assets.
pdf2md-page inline asset placeholders must follow RULE 8 in skills/pdf2md-page/SKILL.md.
Figure placeholders require the uppercase FIGURE: prefix.
Table placeholders require the uppercase TABLE: prefix immediately above the GFM or HTML transcription.
Generic image placeholders use a descriptor plus a suffix such as logo, emblem, seal, cover, photograph, photo, or image.
rewrite_inline_asset_refs.py only rewrites canonical inline asset placeholder shapes.
Placeholder drift forms are surfaced as stderr warnings rather than silently rewritten.
Missing input files require run_status FAILED_INPUTS, empty assets, and an issue naming the missing input.
A page with no extractable assets requires run_status NO_ASSETS, empty assets, and no invented placeholders.
An unreadable page image requires run_status FAILED, empty assets, and an issue explaining the problem.
Partial table uncertainty returns SUCCESS with needs_extraction true, no table_data, and an explicit issue.
PDF2MD, not pdf2md-page-assets, runs materialize_page_assets.py on every page asset JSON.
PDF2MD confirms crop PNGs exist for all non-skipped figure, image, and table records.
PDF2MD confirms table XLSX files exist for table records carrying table_data.
Records flagged needs_extraction true are exempt from table XLSX requirements.
PDF2MD aggregates the document asset manifest.
PDF2MD runs validate_assets.py against the final assembled Markdown.
Unresolved asset references are degraded output requiring human acknowledgment before downstream use.
The pdf2md-page-assets skill identifies visible figures, tables, and meaningful images on one rasterized prose PDF page.
The pdf2md-page-assets skill emits bbox-normalized asset records for deterministic materialization.
The pdf2md-page-assets skill is invoked by PDF2MD asset-enabled mode after per-page Markdown cleanup.
The skill identifies extractable assets on one rasterized prose-document PDF page.
A fig asset is a captioned figure, diagram, plot, chart, plate, or illustration.
A tbl asset is tabular data that should exist as a structured auditable artifact rendered as XLSX downstream.
An img asset is a meaningful non-figure image such as a logo, cover, photograph, or uncaptioned visual object.
The skill reads one page image plus the page cleaned Markdown context and writes one JSON file.
Cropping images, rendering XLSX files, rewriting Markdown links, assembling manifests, and validating filesystem references are deterministic PDF2MD tool responsibilities.
The suitable agent shell is TASK in generic shell mode spawned by the PDF2MD orchestrator.
The pdf2md-page-assets skill is not suitable for whole-PDF conversion.
The pdf2md-page-assets skill is not suitable for cross-page asset stitching.
The pdf2md-page-assets skill is not suitable for deterministic filename assignment.
The pdf2md-page-assets skill is not suitable for cropping, XLSX creation, Markdown rewriting, or manifest aggregation.
Required runtime overrides are IMAGE_PATH, PAGE_MD_PATH, OUTPUT_PATH, DOC_STEM, PAGE_NUM, and TOTAL_PAGES.
IMAGE_PATH is the absolute path to the page PNG.
PAGE_MD_PATH is the absolute path to cleaned per-page Markdown.
OUTPUT_PATH is the absolute path for the asset JSON.
DOC_STEM is the document stem used by downstream deterministic naming tools.
PAGE_NUM is the 1-indexed page number.
TOTAL_PAGES is the total page count of the document.
ASSET_POLICY is optional and defaults to prose-document-assets-v1.
Reads are limited to exactly IMAGE_PATH and PAGE_MD_PATH.
The skill must not read neighbouring pages, manifests, sibling Markdown files, or previously materialized assets.
The read boundary preserves page-level parallelism.
Writes are limited to exactly OUTPUT_PATH.
The output filename is supplied by the orchestrator and must not be derived or changed by the skill.
The pdf2md-page-assets skill uses no deterministic tools.
The allowed-tools frontmatter field is intentionally omitted.
The agent uses native multimodal reading for IMAGE_PATH, native text reading for PAGE_MD_PATH, and native writing for OUTPUT_PATH.
The worker must not crop images.
The worker must not write PNG, CSV, or XLSX files.
The worker must not emit the legacy csv_text field on table records.
The canonical table representation is the structured table_data block.
The worker must not rewrite page Markdown.
The worker must not assign final filenames.
The worker must not widen read or write scope beyond the declared page files.
Input validation confirms IMAGE_PATH exists and has a PNG extension.
Input validation confirms PAGE_MD_PATH exists and has a Markdown extension.
Input validation confirms the OUTPUT_PATH parent exists.
When required inputs are missing, the worker writes valid JSON with run_status FAILED_INPUTS and an empty assets list.
The worker reads PAGE_MD_PATH first to understand captions or inline tables already present in text.
The worker reads IMAGE_PATH and inspects the page visually.
The worker identifies every visible asset that should remain auditable outside plain Markdown.
The worker preserves document reading order within each page.
The worker writes only JSON, with no Markdown fences or commentary.
Top-level JSON field names are exactly schema_version, run_status, doc_stem, page, total_pages, asset_policy, assets, and issues.
The top-level page field must not be named page_num.
The schema_version value must be the literal string pdf2md-page-assets/v1.
run_status must be SUCCESS, NO_ASSETS, FAILED, or FAILED_INPUTS.
The worker must not substitute run_status synonyms such as ok, success, or done.
The assets field is a flat array.
The worker must not add a sibling tables array because tables are entries inside assets with kind tbl.
Per-asset kind must be one of fig, tbl, or img.
Per-asset kind must not use aliases such as figure, image, table, diagram, plot, chart, logo, or photo.
Per-asset bbox_norm must be a four-element JSON array [x0, y0, x1, y1].
Per-asset bbox_norm must not be a JSON object with named coordinate keys.
Per-asset captions must go in the caption field, not label, title, or name.
bbox_norm should generously include the full asset, its visible caption, and a small margin.
Including extra whitespace in bbox_norm is preferred over clipping a figure or caption.
Every legibly extractable tbl asset must emit a table_data object.
The table_data block is the canonical hashable artifact for a table.
Downstream tools render XLSX deterministically from table_data.
If a visible table cannot be transcribed with confidence, the worker omits table_data entirely.
If a visible table cannot be transcribed with confidence, the worker emits needs_extraction true and an issue such as table_unreadable.
The table_data.schema_version field is required and must be the literal pdf2md-table/v1.
The table_data.header_rows field is required and counts leading header rows.
header_rows must be at least 0 and no greater than len(rows).
The table_data.section_dividers field is required and lists row indices where visible internal section breaks appear.
No table merge may cross a section_dividers boundary.
The table_data.continuation_of field is required and is null for standalone tables.
continuation_of identifies an earlier page table when the current table continues it.
The table_data.footnotes field is required and is an array of marker and text objects.
Footnote markers are literal strings that appear on cells referencing the footnote.
The table_data.rows field is required and contains at least one row when the table is extractable.
Each table_data row is an object with a cells array.
Each table_data cell is an object.
A table_data cell value is required and must be a JSON primitive or null.
A null table_data cell value is used only when type is missing.
Cell row_span defaults to 1 and is omitted when the span is 1.
Cell col_span defaults to 1 and is omitted when the span is 1.
Cells covered by a span do not appear separately.
Cell is_header defaults to false and may be omitted when false.
Header cells are bolded by the renderer.
Cell type defaults to text and may be text, number, fraction, missing, formula, or boolean.
Cell unit is optional and carries a unit string for typed numerics.
Cell raw is optional and preserves verbatim perceived text when typing alters the surface form.
Cell footnote_markers is an optional list of marker strings attached to the cell.
Each cell footnote_markers entry must match an entry in the table-level footnotes array.
The text cell type represents a free-form string and is the default.
The number cell type represents clean numeric values and should pair with unit when a unit is shown.
The fraction cell type preserves mixed fractions as strings.
The fraction cell type can use raw to preserve quote-as-inch markers.
The missing cell type uses value null.
The missing cell type can use raw to record surface markers such as em dash, N/A, or blank.
The formula cell type keeps formulas as strings.
The boolean cell type represents true or false values such as checkmarks versus blanks.
table_data.rows length must be at least one when table_data is present.
table_data.header_rows must be between 0 and len(rows), inclusive.
Every section_dividers index must be within [0, len(rows)).
For each table row, emitted cells and covered span cells must sum to the table column count.
row_span may not cross a section_dividers boundary.
Every footnote_markers entry must appear in the table-level footnotes array.
continuation_of.doc_stem should match the current DOC_STEM unless the table truly originates from a different source document.
Asset kind must be exactly fig, tbl, or img.
Asset ordinal is 1-indexed within page and kind in reading order.
Asset caption should use the visible caption when present.
Asset caption should use a concise visual description when no visible caption is present.
Asset slug is advisory only because downstream tools normalize it and append it to a stable ID.
bbox_norm is [x0, y0, x1, y1] in normalized page coordinates with top-left origin.
bbox_norm must be a four-element JSON array rather than a dictionary.
bbox_norm must include the full asset, visible caption, and a small surrounding whitespace margin.
Generous bboxes are preferred because clipped figures or truncated captions are defects.
table_data is required for tbl assets when the table is legibly extractable.
A table_data block must conform to the documented schema.
needs_extraction true is required on visible tbl entries whose cells cannot be safely transcribed.
When needs_extraction true is used, table_data must be omitted entirely.
The legacy csv_text field is removed and must not be emitted.
Downstream materialization rejects any record carrying csv_text.
If no assets are visible, the worker returns run_status NO_ASSETS with an empty assets list.
The pdf2md-page-assets skill has single page in, one JSON out as a non-negotiable constraint.
The worker must not use cross-page context.
The worker must not materialize assets.
The worker must not invent assets or table values.
Every emitted asset must be visible on the page image.
The JSON must parse with standard json.loads.
The output path must exist and be non-empty after a run.
The output JSON must parse successfully.
The output run_status must be SUCCESS, NO_ASSETS, FAILED, or FAILED_INPUTS.
Every emitted asset must have valid kind, ordinal, caption, bbox_norm, and confidence.
Every table asset must include either schema-conforming table_data or needs_extraction true with an explicit issue.
The preferred workflow is reasoning-first: read cleaned page Markdown, inspect the page PNG multimodally, then write one JSON file.
Deterministic tools run outside pdf2md-page-assets under the PDF2MD orchestrator.
tools/pdf2md/build_page_assets_brief.py renders the dispatch brief.
tools/pdf2md/materialize_page_assets.py crops images, delegates table XLSX rendering, and writes anchored page Markdown.
tools/pdf2md/render_table_xlsx.py renders one deterministic XLSX per table_data block.
tools/pdf2md/aggregate_asset_manifest.py merges page manifests.
tools/pdf2md/validate_assets.py validates final references.
There is no TASK-enforced deterministic allowlist for pdf2md-page-assets.
The allowed-tools frontmatter field is intentionally omitted for pdf2md-page-assets.
No operational deterministic tools are invoked inside the pdf2md-page-assets skill.
Operational deterministic tools are invoked by PDF2MD rather than by the page-assets worker.
Reasoning is limited to visual asset identification, bbox estimation, caption and slug proposal, confidence labeling, and table_data transcription.
The worker may use PAGE_MD_PATH only as context for visible captions or already-transcribed tables.
The page image remains the authority for asset existence.
The worker must not write PNG files.
The worker must not write CSV or XLSX files.
The worker must not emit legacy csv_text because table_data is the canonical table representation.
The worker must not rewrite Markdown.
The worker must not aggregate manifests.
The worker must not validate final filesystem references.
The worker must not read files outside IMAGE_PATH and PAGE_MD_PATH.
The worker must not write files outside OUTPUT_PATH.
The worker must not assign final stable filenames.
The tool-policy write boundary is limited to OUTPUT_PATH.
The output filename is deterministic from the orchestrator brief.
The skill must not derive or modify the output filename.
